newsitem.title: UK: World oil supplies rocket in Dec, more to come - IEA.
newsitem.headline: World oil supplies rocket in Dec, more to come - IEA.

text.p: World oil supplies rocketed in December with the help of rising non-OPEC supplies and the return of Iraqi crude, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday.
The Paris-based world energy watchdog also cited prospects for further gains in oil output by producers outside the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).
December world oil production jumped 1.3 million barrels per day (bpd) to 74.7 million, the IEA said in its Monthly Oil Market Report for December.

"New fields in the North Sea and elsewhere, seasonally higher flows in the northern hemisphere and the lack of maintenance activities raised non-OPEC supply to a new high of 45.4 million bpd in December," the IEA said.
North Sea and Latin American crude oil production increased in December by an estimated 700,000 bpd, the IEA said. North Sea output broke seven million bpd for the first time. China also pumped more.
The agency said it expected non-OPEC supplies to shoot up by a full two million bpd this year to 45.6 million bpd with almost half the extra volume coming from the North Sea.
However, it revised down its estimate of non-OPEC supply at the fourth quarter of 1996 by 300,000 bpd to 44.6 million bpd after delays in some North Sea oilfield start-ups.
By contrast, the agency said it had revised downward its estimate for the rise in world demand this year by 200,000 bpd to 73.6 million, for a 1.9 million bpd rise on the year.
It said fourth quarter world demand ran 300,000 bpd lower than estimated in its previous report at 73.6 million.

The agency projected demand for first quarter 1997 at 74.5 million bpd, down 200,000 bpd from last month's forecast. It said the downward demand revisions were largely the result of a reassessment of the supply/demand balance for the former Soviet Union.
Its estimate for apparent demand in the former Soviet Union in the fourth quarter was reduced by 500,000 bpd to 4.3 million.
Demand for OPEC crude was likely to prove 200,000 bpd lower than previously estimated at an average 25.0 million, 1.6 million bpd lower than the group pumped in December, the IEA said.
